summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 4 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.43/1871)

data.turoyo: Annaqqa u ḥakəm uṯewo kušafwo w samwo ‘kašəf rapori‘ bəṯər mu ‘kašəf rapori‘ manṭenawo səhuḏe, səhḏinawo, ka ənnu u zlamano, u malano d flan ḥa yo w səhḏiwole bi maḥkame w ubowa qarar.
data.translation: Then the judge would come, inspect it and make an ‘inspection report’; after the ‘inspection report’ we would bring witnesses, we would testify that this man, this property belonged to such-and-such a person, and they would testify to it in court, and he would give a decision.

rationale: New judicial inspection sense and first Infectum-wa box. English: supplied project machine translation.

summary: New sense 4: (Grundstücke) amtlich besichtigen, untersuchen
rationale: Judge, title-deed claim, boundaries and inspection report establish judicial site inspection; one clear attestation. Medical sense 2 is narrower and remains uncertain.

summary: New sense 4: (Detrans.) enthüllt werden, zutage treten
rationale: Uncovering and coming into the open are coordinated; this is not inherited Detransitive box sense 3 invention. Label 4 follows that inherited cross-key without renumbering it.

data.turoyo: Harke, awwəl naqla kšif w nafəq li ḥolo ftiḥo.
data.translation: Here, for the first time, it was uncovered and came into the open.

rationale: New Detransitive disclosure sense. English: supplied project machine translation.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 4.I/436)

data.turoyo: Hano bu tarix kətle wariḏe yarixe. Hani hul d lə šurenalən w d lə kušfinalən w gulena aʕlayye, kəmarno zaḥme gədhowe lu Alyas, l əno, lu aḥunano, lu aḥuno ḥreno, l ġer aḥnone aḏiʕət, d kkəṯwi hawxa bas l ruḥayye.
data.translation: This has long roots in history. Until we untie them, uncover them and reveal them, I say it will be difficult for Alyas, for me, for this brother, for the other brother, for other brothers, you know, who write like this just for themselves.

rationale: First active I.1 Infectum context; abstract historical roots as object. English: supplied project machine translation.

summary: All three full occurrences are exact inherited example passages, so no additional quotation, numbered sense or stem is justified.
I.1 self-revelation has ruḥux as the reflexive object of Kšaf, parallel to Mbayan ruḥux. The source does not require physical nakedness, and the existing sense already covers revealing.

I.2 kušafla is a dependent Infectum with doctor as subject and daughter -la as patient. Its coordination with seeing and making məʕayana leaves physical uncovering versus medical examination unresolved; retain the inherited question marks.
Detransitive Preterit kšif at 3/45 has an unexpressed inventor and an introduced device patient. Initial k belongs to the root; it is not evidence of an Infectum or ko-Preterit prefix.
Masculine-shaped/default kšif before feminine makkina needs agreement review; no source repair to kšifo is made.
The existing Detransitive example retains active counterpart sense number 3 as printed; no new invention sense is introduced merely to repeat that example.
Raw inherited Imperative is a heading alias of Imperativ; it does not establish a new box. Existing glosses and embedded editorial wording in the medical example are preserved.
No light-verb collocation, participant extension requiring a new sense, or independent additional idiom is established.

Second round, Jan Beṯ-Şawoce. English quotations are the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation; semantic decisions are based on the Turoyo. Earlier-round proposals are inherited for context only and are not repeated in this JSON.
Official judicial inspection is one attested technical use; kašəf rapori is a report noun, not a second verbal occurrence or automatically a new light-verb idiom.
Detransitive label 3 in inherited boxes refers back to active invention sense 3. The added Detransitive disclosure is numbered 4 without changing that inherited cross-reference.
k is the initial root consonant in kšif, kušafwo, kšafa and kušfinalən. Neither the machine translation nor initial k alone identifies an indicative prefix.
Abstract historical roots are an object extension of active I.1 uncovering. Jan does not settle the old medical examination versus physically uncovering question.
In 24/70 does kušafla mean physically uncover the patient before examination, or perform the medical examination? The surrounding məʕayana phrase and edition aufdecken do not resolve this.
At 3/45 is kšif a default/impersonal Detransitive predicate before postposed feminine makkina, or does the edition omit expected feminine -o? Verify without normalizing the supplied form.
Does the team prefer an explicit Detransitive sense-3 heading for erfunden werden, or retain the inherited cross-keying to active sense 3?
